title: Ancient Greece: Teachers of Conquerors
description: From a condemned teacher to a conquering king—five links in a chain of mentors.

questions.question: Who was the most famous student of Socrates?
questions.explanation: After Socrates was executed in 399 BC, Plato turned his teacher's conversations into the dialogues that still anchor Western philosophy.

questions.question: Plato founded a school in a sacred grove outside Athens called what?
questions.explanation: The grove was named for the hero Akademos—and every 'academy' since borrows the name.

questions.question: Which future philosopher studied at Plato's Academy for about twenty years?
questions.explanation: Aristotle arrived around age 17 and stayed until Plato died in 347 BC—then went on to disagree with his teacher about almost everything.

questions.question: King Philip II of Macedon hired Aristotle to tutor which teenage prince?
questions.explanation: From about 343 BC, Aristotle taught the young Alexander—who would carry Greek culture from Egypt to India.

questions.question: As a boy, Alexander the Great tamed a horse no one else could ride—what was its name?
questions.explanation: Alexander noticed the horse was afraid of its own shadow and turned it toward the sun. He later named a city in its honor.
